newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on profit-taking.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended sharply down on Friday on panic profit-taking triggered by overnight losses on the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active March 1997 contract ended at 20,980 yuan ($2,527) per tonne, losing 400 yuan. It opened at an intra-day high of 21,380 and hit a low of 20,900.
December fell 110 to 20,640, January 300 to 20,900, February 390 to 21,000, April 410 to 20,970 and May 270 to 21,030.
Combined volume fell to 69,860 tonnes from 142,920.
Copper opened mostly lower and dropped for most of the session.
Traders said LME losses and an overbought technical index discouraged long position holders, with long liquidation dominating today's trade.
"Most retail investors offset their long positions in case of further falls in the next few days," one trader said.
"Panic selling emerged in the morning session, resulting in sharp falls today," he added.
Traders said the future direction will depend on copper's performance on Monday.
"The rebound is likely to finish if copper cannot recover most of its losses next Monday," a second trader said. "But copper really needs to correct its recent sharp rise."
Analysts said Shanghai copper will closely follow movements in the LME in the next few trading days due in the absence of domestic market-moving news.
Aluminium ended mixed in slow trading. December was unchanged at 13,910, January rose 50 to 14,150 and February fell 100 to 14,200. Combined volume fell to 850 tonnes from 2,360.
